sections.title: Why Troubleshooting Matters at This Level
learningObjectives: Understand the scope of operator-level troubleshooting
Recognize the boundary between operator response and technician diagnosis
sections.content: This module covers recognizing and responding to common issues, not fixing them. Deep diagnostic work belongs to L3A (Technician level) - your job at L2 is to recognize when something's wrong, categorize it well enough to communicate clearly, and know when to escalate rather than attempt a fix.

keyTerms.note: MoRo's Human-Machine Interface (HMI) platform, used for fleet monitoring, mission control, and programming.

sections.title: A Structured Approach to Diagnosis
learningObjectives: Understand a basic structured approach to noticing and describing a problem at operator level
Know what information to gather before escalating
sections.content: When something goes wrong, a simple structured approach helps: what was MoRo doing right before the issue appeared, what does its current status show, and has anything changed in the environment (new obstruction, relocated equipment)? Gathering these details before escalating makes the technician's diagnosis faster once it's handed off.

video.title: When something goes wrong in 30 seconds
video.transcript: When something goes wrong, in 30 seconds. At L2 you recognize, categorize and know when to escalate. You do not attempt the fix. Ask: what was MoRo doing just before? What does its status show now? Has anything changed around it? Share those details when you escalate.

sections.title: Sensor-Related Issues
learningObjectives: Recognize general symptoms of a sensor-related issue
sections.content: Sensor issues (LiDAR obstruction, unexpected stops in areas that should be clear) often present as MoRo behaving overly cautious or stopping where it shouldn't need to. Check for obvious causes first - something physically blocking a sensor - but don't attempt sensor cleaning or adjustment yourself unless specifically trained and authorized to do so; escalate instead.

sections.title: Communication Errors
learningObjectives: Recognize general symptoms of a connectivity-related issue
sections.content: MoRo depends on network connectivity to communicate with the fleet system and ANT server. A unit that becomes unresponsive on the dashboard, or that stops accepting new mission assignments, may indicate a connectivity issue rather than a hardware fault. Note when this started and escalate - connectivity troubleshooting generally falls outside operator-level response.

sections.title: Mission Failures Revisited
learningObjectives: Recall the categories of mission failure introduced in L2-M1
Apply the structured approach to mission failures specifically
sections.content: L2-M1 introduced the basic response to a failed mission: note, assess safety, escalate. Applying this module's structured approach, a mission failure diagnosis benefits from noting whether it failed at the start, mid-route, or at the destination - that detail alone significantly narrows down likely causes for whoever picks up the diagnosis.

sections.title: When to Escalate
learningObjectives: Understand the general threshold for escalation versus self-resolution
Know what information to include when escalating
sections.content: As a general rule: if an issue resolves on its own within a normal operational pattern (a brief pause that clears, a single retry that succeeds), no escalation is needed. If it recurs, persists, or falls outside anything covered in this curriculum, escalate with what you observed - timing, symptoms, anything unusual in the environment. A specific error code reference table is being developed with DiFacto's engineering team and will be added to this module once available.

questions.question: MoRo stops several times at the same spot. Which response fits the L2 role?
options: Work out the fault and fix it before reporting
Note what it was doing, what its status shows and what has changed nearby, then escalate
questions.feedback: Correct. At L2 you recognize and respond. Deep diagnosis belongs to L3A.

questions.question: What information is useful to gather before escalating an issue?
options: What MoRo was doing, its current status, and any environmental changes
Nothing - just escalate immediately and let the technician ask for details
questions.feedback: Correct. This context speeds up the technician's eventual diagnosis.

questions.question: MoRo stops where the path looks clear. What do you check first?
options: Whether the sensor needs cleaning, and clean it
Whether something is physically blocking a sensor
Whether a retry gets it through
questions.feedback: Correct. Check for obvious causes first, such as something physically blocking a sensor. Do not clean or adjust a sensor yourself; escalate instead.

questions.question: A unit stops accepting new missions and is unresponsive on the dashboard. What do you do?
options: Treat it as a hardware fault
Note when it started and escalate
questions.feedback: Correct. This may indicate a connectivity issue rather than a hardware fault.

questions.question: What detail about a mission failure is useful to note for diagnosis?
options: Whether it failed at the start, mid-route, or at the destination
How many missions ran earlier that day
questions.feedback: Correct. Where in the mission it failed significantly narrows down likely causes.
